clue.text: Drink I avoided facing present field of activity

indicators.note: facing puts the two pieces side by side, one meeting the other
avoided means the letter I is kept out of the drink word

parts.note: to sip is to drink a little
present means here, in attendance

explanation.surface: Someone skips a drink while facing up to the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing' only means side by side here, and 'avoided' removes the I that the clue names.
explanation.definitionFit: A sphere is a domain or area of interest, as in a sphere of influence.

clue.text: Wretched boss, right-winger, providing pitiful tale

indicators.note: wretched means in a bad state, so the letters of boss are knocked into disorder

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: A miserable conservative boss offering a hard-luck story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wretched' turns BOSS into SOBS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob story is a sad account told to win sympathy.

clue.text: German mislaid a comb in old form of transport

parts.note: Hans is a typical German man's name

indicators.note: mislaid suggests things put in the wrong place, so the letters of a comb are disordered

explanation.surface: A German lost a comb while riding in an old carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mislaid' turns A COMB into OMCAB.
explanation.definitionFit: A hansom cab was a two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage for hire.

clue.text: Cut down summary having removed chapter

indicators.note: having removed means the chapter letter is taken out of the summary word

parts.note: a recap is a summary

explanation.surface: An abridged summary with one chapter dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to harvest, cutting down crops.

clue.text: Distant century I term largely ridiculous

parts.note: distant means far
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so the final letter of the term word is lost

parts.note: to call something is to term it

explanation.surface: A remote age where one person names things in an absurd way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts CALL to CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Farcical means absurd, like a stage farce.

clue.text: A number of chaps brought up individual plant

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the word is written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: a number of chaps are men
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: Several men raised a lone plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses MEN to NEM in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An anemone is a flowering plant of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Line in a daily act devised to stop work

indicators.note: in means the line letter goes inside the rearranged letters
devised means made up anew, so the letters of a daily act are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A line in a routine invented to knock off for the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' turns A DAILY ACT into CALITADAY, and L goes 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To call it a day is an idiom for finishing work.

clue.text: Mike supporting firm? Funny

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts the mike word underneath the firm word

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
mike and mic are both short for microphone

explanation.surface: A microphone backing a company, comedy perhaps?
explanation.definitionFit: Comic means amusing or humorous.

clue.text: Most recent cocktail at establishment bottled

indicators.note: bottled means the letters are stored inside the words cocktail at establishment

explanation.surface: The newest cocktail at a bar is sold in bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Latest means newest, the most up to date.

clue.text: Perhaps ace distinction

definitions.meaning: in bridge the ace is one of the top-ranking cards, with king, queen, jack and ten
an award or mark of high esteem

explanation.definitionFit: In bridge the high cards bear this title, and an award or privilege is also one.

clue.text: Move along in poor Indian city

indicators.note: in puts the shuffled letters inside the word for poor

parts.note: bare means poor, meagre, as in a bare living

indicators.note: move tells us to shift the letters of the following word around

explanation.surface: An instruction to shift on, given in a deprived part of an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but it is the container: the shuffled letters split the word for poor after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore, now Bengaluru, is a large city in southern India.

clue.text: Restrict road entering place for retirement in France

indicators.note: entering means the road abbreviation goes inside the French word

parts.note: lit is French for bed, where one retires at night
MI, the M1, is Britain's main motorway, a common crossword road

explanation.surface: Limiting traffic on a road that leads to a French retirement spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' here means going to bed, not leaving work.
explanation.definitionFit: To limit something is to restrict or cap it.

clue.text: Seat lacking in second plane, perhaps

indicators.note: lacking in means the seat word goes without the letter for second

parts.note: a stool is a seat

explanation.surface: A seat with something missing on a second aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' is the woodworker's tool, not an aircraft; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter's plane is one example of a hand implement.

clue.text: Lose the ability to cope having got nothing with bishops, say

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing
bishops are one kind of chess piece; say marks the example

explanation.surface: Someone breaks down after ending up with nothing but bishops.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pieces is an idiom for collapsing emotionally under stress.

clue.text: Withdrawal from English university during holiday

indicators.note: during means the university letter sits within the holiday word

parts.note: a vacation is a holiday

explanation.surface: Leaving an English university in the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Evacuation is the removal of people from a place.

clue.text: Get back position in field after leaders in race emerge

indicators.note: after puts the fielding word behind the opening letters
leaders in means the opening letters of the next two words

parts.note: cover is a fielding position in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone retakes their spot in the field once the front runners appear.
explanation.walkthrough: COVER is a cricket fielding position on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover is to regain or retrieve something lost.

clue.text: Celebrity among the Spanish showing glossy surface

indicators.note: among puts the celebrity word inside the Spanish article

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
a big name is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A famous figure among the Spanish showing off a shiny finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a hard glassy coating, as on pottery or teeth.

clue.text: Red wine spilt around party? It's found over bed

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go about the party word
spilt means the letters of red wine are splashed about into new order

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Red wine knocked over at a party, landing on the bedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' turns RED WINE into EIDERWN, placed 'around' DO.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt filled with down feathers laid on a bed.

clue.text: Tender support and love associated with girl

parts.note: a prop is a support
love is zero in tennis, written O
Sal is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A gentle young man with backing and love for a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' is the noun, an offer, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is a formal offer, such as a bid for a contract.

clue.text: A vehicle skirting a city, initially? One can count on it

indicators.note: skirting means the vehicle word goes around the opening letters

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A bus going round the edge of a town at the start of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes A and C from 'a city'; BUS goes round them.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads used for arithmetic.

clue.text: Gratify fully a set casually eating starters in trattoria in August

indicators.note: eating means the jumbled letters take the starters inside them
casually means the letters of a set are thrown together loosely in new order
starters in means the first letters of the next three words

explanation.surface: A group dining informally on starters at an Italian restaurant in summer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casually' makes SATE from A SET; it takes in TIA, the 'starters in' trattoria in August.
explanation.definitionFit: To satiate is to satisfy completely, filling to the full.

clue.text: Hebridean, say, rejecting leader? A defamatory statement

indicators.note: rejecting leader means the first letter of the islander word is dropped

parts.note: someone from the Hebrides, Scottish islands, is an islander; say marks the example

explanation.surface: A Scottish islander turning down a chief while making false claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting leader' drops the I from ISLANDER. The Hebrides are islands off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Slander is a spoken false claim that harms someone's reputation.

clue.text: Sun continually seen over northern river

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Sun, as in Sunday
ever means always, continually

explanation.surface: Always seeing the sun above the northern river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Severn is Britain's longest river, flowing through Wales and England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is a British waterway.

clue.text: Guitarist with explosive bit of music producing havoc

parts.note: Brian May is the guitarist of the rock band Queen
HE is short for high explosive

indicators.note: bit of means just the first letter of music

explanation.surface: A guitarist with a blast of music causing chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem means chaos and disorder.

clue.text: Alluring tie and cravat crumpled round back of closet

indicators.note: round means the jumbled letters wrap around the final letter
crumpled means the letters of tie and cravat are crushed into a new order
back of means the last letter of the word closet

explanation.surface: Neckwear left creased around the rear of a wardrobe looks appealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumpled' rearranges the neckwear into ATTRACIVE; 'round' wraps that around the last letter that 'back of' takes from closet.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractive means appealing or pleasing to look at.

clue.text: Fool accepting singular distortion

indicators.note: accepting means the fool word takes the singular letter inside it

parts.note: a twit is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool taking on an odd misrepresentation.
explanation.definitionFit: A twist is a bending or warping of the truth or a shape.

clue.text: Supply hunting whip

definitions.meaning: a harvest, a yield or stock of produce
a short riding whip with a loop, carried when riding to hounds

explanation.definitionFit: A crop is both a harvest gathered as a stock and a riding switch used in fox hunting.

clue.text: A group on board reduced measure of land

indicators.note: reduced means the crew word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a crew is the group working on board a ship

explanation.surface: A ship's crew cut down to a smaller piece of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts CREW to CRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area.

clue.text: Hot couple of islands? No, part of one in the Caribbean

definitions.text: part of one in the Caribbean

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
an ait is a small river island
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: Is this hot spot two islands? No, it shares one in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: An AIT (or eyot) is a small island in a river, a British word. The country shares the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic, hence 'part of one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Haiti occupies the western third of Hispaniola, a Caribbean island.

clue.text: Cairo's out for recreation? Appalling

indicators.note: recreation read as re-creation means making the letters over again in a new order

parts.note: the city name with its S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: Egypt's capital is out of bounds for leisure, which is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'recreation' as re-creation: CAIROSOUT is re-formed. The 's of Cairo's gives a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocious means shockingly bad or dreadful.

clue.text: Greek character in front of entire ground, revolting type

indicators.note: in front of puts the Greek letter before the jumbled piece

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: ground means crushed up, so the letters of entire are broken and remixed

explanation.surface: A Greek figure leading a whole stretch of land, a rebellious sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' turns ENTIRE into TINEER; 'revolting' means rebelling, not disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutineer is one who rebels against those in command.

clue.text: Man and woman endlessly in home for Dane?

parts.note: Ken is a man's name

indicators.note: endlessly means the woman's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Nell is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A couple keeping house forever, perhaps a Danish couple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dane' is a Great Dane, the dog; the question mark flags the trick. 'endlessly' cuts NELL to NEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A kennel is a dog's shelter, and a Great Dane is a dog breed.
